subject: MSA/DPA/Order Form cutover coordination — sequencing & acceptance gates
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Michael Bailey <michael.bailey@heliomed.ai>, Helio Procurement <procurement@heliomed.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/DPA/Order Form cutover coordination — sequencing & acceptance gates

Hi Michael / Procurement team,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per follow-up, I sketched a suggested cutover sequencing that keeps your pilot evaluation running while we finalize the MSA/DPA and the Order Form. The goals are: protect data during the pilot, keep the evaluation KPIs stable, and avoid rework when signatures land. Key proposed sequence: 

- Week 0 (pilot running): continue on hosted sandbox; we enable request-level logging and token retention = 30d (pilot-only)
- Week 1: legal review window — Helio and Redwood redlines reviewed in parallel; both sides designate a single SME for each clause
- Week 2: commercial finalize Order Form (pricing/seat counts, start date) — sign tentative order form (subject to final legal) to reserve Dedicated capacity start date
- Week 3: execute DPA + MSA signatures, Order Form converted to final; production cutover scheduled 7 days after signature with a dry-run 48h prior

I've attached an annotated MSA (Helio-MSA_annotated_v2.pdf) and a draft order form template (OrderForm-Proposal-Helio.docx) so your team can see what fields we need locked. 

Questions for you before I share this with legal: 
1) Who at Helio will serve as the single legal SME for redlines?
2) Do you need the Order Form to include a pilot discount or an explicit pilot-to-production price ladder?
3) Are there any procurement lead times (PO windows) that would force us to shift the cutover date?

If you prefer, Jordan can run the commercial items and Karthik will take the legal redlines. I’ll coordinate the tech cutover checklist.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

Thanks Irene — this looks clear and sensible. Quick answers: 

- Legal SME: Maria Gonzalez (maria.gonzalez@heliomed.ai) will shepherd redlines on our side. She prefers a single redline doc + summary comments.
- Pilot pricing: Procurement would like the pilot discount recorded in the Order Form as an explicit line item (so we can reference it in PO processing).
- PO lead time: Typical PO cycle is 3–4 weeks once commercial terms are agreed; if we can lock commercial terms this week, procurement can accelerate approval but needs the draft Order Form fields final.

We'd like to avoid delaying the pilot. If you can give a 48h turnaround on redline responses, we should be OK. I'll loop Maria into the thread.

Best,

Folks — attaching my redline bundle (redlines_karthik_20260519.docx) and a short checklist of gating items. A few legal comments to flag up front: 

- Liability cap: propose we keep the mutual liability cap at 1x/12 months of forecasted fees for pilot, with a production uplift as part of the final Order Form.
- Data processing locations: agree to note US-only for pilot and a separate annex for EU residency if/when Helio moves EU subject data into production.
- Audit logs: offer 90-day retention by default; 365-day option available as a paid add-on.

Gating checklist (high level):
1) Commercial — signed Order Form with pilot discount line (Jordan)
2) Legal — executed MSA + DPA (Karthik / Maria)
3) Procurement — PO or internal approval recorded (Helio procurement)
4) Tech — dry-run completed + KV cache wipe plan (Irene)

Irene — recommend a single 48h test window (dry-run) before cutover to validate routing and KV hygiene. If Helio can sign the Order Form by Friday (May 22), we can still target production cutover the following week.

-Karthik
General Counsel (contracts) | Redwood Inference
